name: ActionPulse
description: Local-first task cockpit that helps you start: explainable urgency scoring, one-thing focus mode, LAN sync, zero-dependency backend.

paragraphs: A local-first task cockpit that turns I do not know where to start into I am already doing it.
features: Weights are covered by unit tests that assert the documented ordering actually holds (a high + overdue task must outrank a low + someday one), so the formula cannot silently drift.

A full-screen stage that shows exactly one task. Everything else disappears. Hit not this one to swap it out, or done to move on. If the task feels too big, break it into 3–5 micro-steps in place — offline verb…
When the top of your list all feels equally impossible, roll the dice. It picks one task from your top three and drops you straight into focus mode.
The roll is weighted by urgency, not uniform — a uniform 1-in-3 roll would throw away the entire ranking. You get randomness to break the paralysis, without discarding the algorithm.

The hardest part of any task is the first two minutes. Start a 120-second timer with the prompt just do two minutes — you can stop after. When it rings you can stop, or one tap refills it into a full 25-minute pomodoro…

whatItDoes.text: A local-first task cockpit that turns I do not know where to start into I am already doing it.

requirements.text: Nothing else — no database, no Docker, no account.
There is no cloud, no account, and no server you do not own.
